Adding a data point from the post-settlement reconciliation side (`quote-lock` -> conditional split -> ledger reconciliation).

In practice, we've found the split between **evidence capture** and **adjudication/reconciliation** described earlier in this thread holds up cleanly when implemented as two separate steps:

changes.author: zambodotdev
changes.text:
Data point lands on the right side of the split this thread settled on: evidence capture and adjudication as separate steps, neither one trusting mutable API state.

Your quote lock is the pre-execution mirror of the receipt problem. You commit a canonical hash of the terms before execution, so the later comparison has something fixed to compare against. Same reason a receipt hashes the saved result at job time: adjudication is only as good as the commitment it checks against.
